SMTO-CTR-0024 — A check found parts of the task plan that don't fit together

GUID: 024f84e8-2530-4ef5-8f48-7c9d9f43c438
Slug: task-contract-structure-invalid
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: ctr

What happened

  • A separate check of a Task Contract (the step-by-step plan SMTO writes from a request) found items that repeat, point to missing items, or wait on each other in a circle. The check didn't run or change anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details to see which problem was found: a repeated item, a link to a missing item, steps waiting on each other in a circle, or mismatched questions. The named problem tells whoever reviews the plan exactly which part is broken.
  2. Send the original request again so SMTO writes a new Task Contract. Don't submit this same plan again unchanged. An unchanged plan fails the same check every time, while a newly written plan gets checked from scratch.

What success looks like

  • The check passes for the new Task Contract, or the new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • If new plans keep showing the same problem, select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat a plan that failed this check as approved to run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Offline TaskContract structure validation rejected the contract for duplicate IDs, references to missing items, a stage dependency cycle, or a clarification flag that disagrees with its questions.

What this means

  • Contract structure validation finds duplicate IDs, missing cross-references, a dependency cycle or inconsistent clarification flags/questions. This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.

Why this can happen

  • Contract structure validation finds duplicate IDs, missing cross-references, a dependency cycle or inconsistent clarification flags/questions.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific structural rule in model/offline validation; the current compiler acceptance gate does not enforce this entire schema.

How to fix it

  • Read the specific rule in the error text (duplicate_id, invalid_reference, dependency_cycle or clarification_invalid) and correct that part of the contract, or regenerate it from the original source. TaskContract.validate_structure in src/agent_runtime/native/task_contract_models.py is an optional offline diagnostic (used by scripts/task_contract_benchmark.py and fixtures), not the compiler acceptance gate, and passing it never authorizes execution.
  • Use the supported contract correction flow to repair the named structural defect without treating it as execution authority.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The explicitly inspected contract satisfies its declared internal structure.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
